picks.style: doric victory ode, kithara and double aulos, layered male chorus, stately, processional, blazing
picks.why: 'Water is best, and gold, like a blazing fire in the night' — the most famous opening in Greek lyric, and a real hymn to the games.

picks.style: ancient greek mystery hymn, lyre and low drone, hushed layered voices, slow, radiant, floating
picks.why: The Isle of the Blessed — equal nights and days, ocean breezes, flowers of gold blazing on land and in water.

picks.style: symposium ode, lyre and soft flutes, warm generous tenor, unhurried, celebratory, golden
picks.why: The golden goblet foaming with wine passed to a son-in-law, and song poured out the same way — one perfect extended simile.

picks.style: renaissance invocation, viol consort and chamber organ, grave declamatory male voice, slow, cosmic, unfolding
picks.why: 'Of shapes transformde to bodies straunge' and then Chaos itself — the poem's opening and its whole programme in one breath.

picks.style: elizabethan pursuit song, lute and bass viol, urgent pleading tenor, driving fourteener swing, breathless
picks.why: Apollo calling after the fleeing Daphne — 'Thou doest not know, poore simple soule, from whome thou fleest'.

picks.style: elizabethan tragic ballad, lute and viol, dark storytelling voice, moonlit, foreboding, moderate
picks.why: Thisbe at Ninus' tomb, the bloody-jawed lioness, the dropped mantle — the turn on which the whole tragedy hinges.

picks.style: english pastoral elegy, harpsichord and flute, clear tenor, unhurried, hopeful with a shadow, strophic
picks.why: 'Stern Winter hence with all his train removes' — a clean spring quatrain sequence that checks its own optimism.

picks.style: languid summer air, viola and guitar, hazy warm voice, slow, heat-struck, still
picks.why: Three hours past noon, the street empty, the ditches dry — concrete, sensory, and unusual as a subject for song.

picks.style: patriotic warning ode, low strings and muffled drum, stern baritone, measured, gathering, ominous
picks.why: A complete sonnet whose sting is the ending: not Spain nor France, 'but from thyself, thy Ruin must proceed'.

picks.style: georgian chamber song, harpsichord and cello, plain warm female voice, moderate, contented, settled
picks.why: A whole life's wish in a dozen lines — quiet retreat, no widow's curse, 'an honest heart is worth its weight in gold'.

picks.style: comic pastoral ballad, fiddle and guitar, mischievous soprano, brisk anapestic lilt, tripping, deadpan
picks.why: The swain who cannot choose between three girls and so 'decently on the green willow expir'd'.

picks.style: birthday air, spinet and recorder, bright light soprano, quick, affectionate, toasting
picks.why: The shortest day of the year explained — the sun stays down and lends his rays to Stella's eyes.

picks.style: augustan satiric march, snare and harpsichord, dry mocking female voice, brisk, strutting, comic
picks.why: Charles XII demolished by his table manners — dirty thumbs on the butter, and 'Eat, and Drink, and Live and Reign in Boots'.

picks.style: mock-martial song, trumpet and strings, bold arch female voice, marching, teasing, spirited
picks.why: British women as the real standing army — 'At Flurt of Fan, our armed Legions fly'.

picks.style: english naval ballad, hornpipe fiddle and drum, hearty chorus voice, rolling, confident, salt-air
picks.why: The sailors 'boisterous as the winds at sea' but 'gentle all, as Southern Gales on Shore' — a ready-made ballad couplet.

picks.style: hellenistic ritual lament, double aulos and frame drum, keening female voice with answering chorus, slow, processional, grieving
picks.why: 'I cry alas for Adonis: fair Adonis is dead' — a refrain that is already a refrain, with the white tusk in the white thigh.

picks.style: greek funeral hymn, lyre and low reed, layered mourning voices, slow, tender, ceremonial
picks.why: Blood becoming the rose and tears the anemone, then 'even a corpse he is fair, a fair corpse, as one asleep'.

picks.style: closing threnody, solo aulos and soft drum, single low female voice fading, very slow, spent, resigned
picks.why: The lament tells itself to stop and promises to begin again next year — the perfect last verse.

picks.style: oracular chant, struck bronze and hollow drone, cavernous whispering male voice, slow, riddling, unsettling
picks.why: Only candidate, but it carries four real Delphic verses — 'best is Fuscus, good the African, worst the White man'.

picks.style: greek rhapsodic fragment, solo lyre, questioning tenor, sparse, hesitant, unresolved
picks.why: Only candidate: a chain of Theban questions that turns on 'My Muse, we're poor in that we are too rich'.
